title: New York City public school time, 2026-27
measure: Scheduled hours in school per year: standard school day length, bell to bell, including lunch and recess, times scheduled student attendance days. This is not New York State's 'instructional hours' measure, which excludes lunch and recess (8 NYCRR 175.5).

core_findings.us_average_basis: 6.9 hours x 178.6 days, typical K-12 public school (traditional and charter), 2017-18 National Teacher and Principal Survey, per Kraft and Novicoff (2025)
core_findings.k12_note: Illustrative: assumes the 2026-27 schedule holds for 13 years and perfect attendance. Years measured in national-average years of 1,231 hours, the convention Kraft and Novicoff use (133 hours x 13 / 1,231 = their '1.4 additional years').

week_grid_2026_27.definition: All five weekdays are full in-person student days for that grade band: no holiday, recess, early dismissal, remote day, staff or clerical day, and for high school no Regents exam day. Computed in index.html from the calendar rules.

comparison_data_2026_27.definition: Scheduled hours in school per year, 2026-27: student days x bell-to-bell day length (including lunch and recess), adjusted for recurring early-dismissal days. Ranges span grade levels or schools. Systems that set hours school by school with no published system-wide schedule are listed but not charted.

systems.name: Success Academy (New York City charter network)
systems.daily_schedule: Elementary 7:50 a.m.-4:20 p.m.; middle 8:00 a.m.-4:00 p.m.; high school 7:55 a.m.-4:30 p.m.; Wednesdays dismiss at 12:50, 12:20 and 1:00 p.m.
systems.first_last_day: Aug. 3 (high school grades 10-12) to Sept. 9 (kindergarten); June 11 for K-8; May 21 to June 17 for high school grades
systems.derivation: Day-by-day count of each grade cohort's 2026-27 network calendar (excluding the Bronx K-12 campus); Wednesdays and start-of-year half days at the Wednesday dismissal time
systems.status: Derived from network calendars and handbook

systems.name: KIPP NYC (charter network, K-8 schools)
systems.daily_schedule: 7 to 8 hours depending on school (e.g., KIPP Star Harlem Middle 8:00 a.m.-3:00 p.m.; KIPP Beyond Middle 7:55 a.m.-3:30 p.m.; KIPP Freedom Middle 7:15 a.m.-3:15 p.m.); eight network-wide 1:30 p.m. early dismissals
systems.derivation: Each school's 2026-27 Student and Family Handbook; high schools not included

systems.name: Chicago Public Schools
systems.daily_schedule: Elementary 7 hours (since 2012; teachers' contract: day 'shall normally begin at 8:30 a.m. and end at 3:30 p.m.'); high school about 7 hours 15 minutes (2024-25 school-profile median, 435 minutes)
systems.status: Derived; high school end uses 2024-25 data

systems.name: Houston ISD
systems.days: 181 (our count of the official calendar; matches Houston Chronicle)
systems.daily_schedule: Set by campus; no district-wide bell schedule found. Campus bell-schedule pages sampled (school year not stated) show 7 to 8.5 hours.
systems.derivation: Not charted. The earlier 1,260 figure is the Texas legal minimum (75,600 minutes), not Houston's schedule.

systems.name: Miami-Dade County Public Schools
systems.daily_schedule: Set by school; elementary grades 2-5 and K-8 centers (grades 2-8) released one hour early every Wednesday
systems.derivation: Not charted: no district-wide bell schedule found

systems.name: Los Angeles Unified School District
systems.daily_schedule: Not verified for 2026-27; the district's 2023 bulletin set minimum instructional minutes (excluding lunch and recess), not bell-to-bell times

systems.name: Uncommon Schools NYC (charter network)
systems.days: About 180-182 elementary and middle; 171-180 high school
systems.daily_schedule: Not published ('campus hours vary by school'); Fridays dismiss at 12:30 p.m.

us_average_reference.name: Typical U.S. public school (2017-18 data)
us_average_reference.source: Kraft and Novicoff, Education Next, Winter 2025

calendar_constraints: Start after Labor Day (NYC Public Schools, citing state Education Law and staff contracts)
End before the second-to-last weekday in June (NYC Public Schools, citing state Education Law and staff contracts)
At least 180 days of session, which may include superintendents' (chancellor's) conference days (Education Law 3604(7); 8 NYCRR 175.5)
A deficiency of up to four days for superintendents' conferences is excused (Education Law 3604(8))
Remote instruction days count as student attendance days (NYC Public Schools)

matthew_kraft.title: Professor of education and economics, Brown University (per Chalkbeat)
matthew_kraft.co_author_of: Time for School (Education Next, Winter 2025), with Sarah Novicoff
matthew_kraft.quote_on_state_minimums: They are not what we should be targeting or aspiring to. They set a floor that we should be moving beyond.
matthew_kraft.quote_context: Said of state laws setting minimum school time; Chalkbeat, Feb. 27, 2026
matthew_kraft.secondary_quote: Overall the evidence strongly points to additional instructional time increasing student success in school. Of course, how much time you add, when you add it, and how it's used also matter tremendously. But it is one of those necessary but not sufficient inputs into supporting a successful education.

david_bloomfield.title: Professor of education, law, and public policy, Brooklyn College and CUNY Graduate Center
david_bloomfield.key_quote: What seems like 180 days isn't really. A child's individual calendar may differ from grade to grade, program to program because of testing and other non-instructional obligations.
david_bloomfield.quote_note: Chalkbeat printed these as two quoted passages separated by 'he said, adding'.
david_bloomfield.fragmentation_observation_paraphrase: Out of 45 school weeks, he said, less than half — about 20 — have complete five-day weeks.
david_bloomfield.fragmentation_note: Chalkbeat paraphrase, not a direct quote; refers to the 2025-26 calendar (Chalkbeat, Feb. 27, 2026).

kamar_samuels.title: New York City Schools Chancellor
kamar_samuels.context: Pledged to focus on chronic absenteeism (Chalkbeat, Feb. 27, 2026)
kamar_samuels.quote: Folks need to understand that if we're not in school your child is going to miss work.

context_data.nyc_chronic_absenteeism: About 1 in 3 New York City students were chronically absent in 2024-25 (Chalkbeat, Feb. 27, 2026)
context_data.ny_state_per_pupil_spending: 91 percent above the national average in 2021-22; estimated $36,293 per student in 2024-25 (Citizens Budget Commission, Jan. 17, 2025; New York State, not New York City)
